WhatsApp launched a username reservation system a few days ago and is now starting to enable the full feature for some users. Details below.

WhatsApp begins activating reserved usernames

WhatsApp launched its username reservation system last month, allowing users to claim a unique username ahead of the full feature rollout.

Users can go to "Settings" > "Account" > "Username" to reserve a username, and can choose to allow anyone who knows their username to contact them, or require new contacts to enter an additional four-digit PIN after entering the username.

When the chosen username matches an account already established on another Meta platform (such as Facebook or Instagram), users may be required to prove they have control of the relevant account. This measure aims to prevent misuse of well-known brand usernames and potential impersonation scams.

However, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now starting to activate reserved usernames for a small number of accounts.

Users included in this initial phase rollout can now see a banner notification at the top of their chat list informing them that their username has been activated and can be shared with new contacts.

The report notes that this feature is being rolled out to both Beta testers and users on the official version of WhatsApp, but emphasises that it currently appears to be limited to a "very small number of users".

To check whether your account has received this feature, look out for the banner notification at the top of your chat list, or go to the "Username" section in your profile settings. That section will indicate whether your username has been activated, or show a message such as "Username coming soon — we'll let you know when it's ready".
